question: Walk me through your most challenging project.
answer: In the AQI project, the real data was messy, with missing pollutant values, zeros and outliers. I imputed missing values city-wise using the median, treated the zeros, and winsorized outliers at the 1st and 99th percentiles. I encoded city and season, added month and season features, and trained XGBoost, which also copes with missing inputs at prediction time. I then deployed it on Streamlit Cloud with a custom UI.

question: Tell me about a time you got stuck on a bug.

I fixed it by casting to int, and now I watch for unsigned arithmetic whenever I loop to size() - k. It taught me to debug by reasoning about the cause instead of guessing.

question: Why did you build the AQI Prediction System?
answer: Calculating AQI with the official formula needs many pollutant values, like PM2.5, PM10, O3 and NH3, and a normal person can't easily find all of them. So I thought, why not train a model on the already available state-wise AQI data and give people a good estimate of the AQI of their place instead.

question: Why did you choose XGBoost for the AQI model?
answer: Real-world pollutant data often has missing values. XGBoost handles missing values on its own, so the model can still give a prediction even when some pollutant readings are unavailable. That was exactly the problem I wanted to solve.

question: What was the biggest challenge in the AQI project?
answer: Making the predictions work when some pollutant readings are missing. I designed the prediction pipeline around that, with the model handling the gaps automatically, so a user doesn't need every sensor value to get an estimate.

question: What did you learn from the Movie Recommendation System?

I built it following a CampusX tutorial, and it was a good way to understand how recommendation systems work end to end.
